overview: A strong early-season storm hits the Sierra and Eastern Sierra Thursday, with a weaker system behind it. Utah and Wyoming get snow Thursday through Saturday as a Pacific trough crosses the West, and the Cascades stay on the drier side until a weak system arrives Saturday night.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong system is moving across the northern Sierra and southern Cascades through Thursday, bringing heavy mountain snow above 4000 feet. Winter storm warnings run until 4 AM Friday, and the strongest winds are expected Thursday afternoon. Kirkwood leads with 17 inches on Thursday alone, and Sugar Bowl and Palisades got a similar big day. Drier weather returns Friday afternoon, with a weaker trough bringing more mountain snow over the weekend.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A potent storm brings heavy Sierra snow, strong winds and hazardous travel through Friday morning. The Sierra crest is the focus, with winds gusting over the ridges. Mammoth gets 13 inches on Thursday and 17 inches over the period. The NWS is calling for more, 19 to 31 inches Thursday through Tuesday night. A brief break Friday afternoon gives way to another system Saturday afternoon.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A storm arrives in pieces from early Thursday through Saturday morning, with the heaviest snow in the northern mountains. Powder Mountain leads with 9 inches on Friday, and Snowbasin got a similar day. The NWS is calling for more, 19 to 36 inches Thursday through Monday. Winter weather advisories are in effect Thursday through Saturday. Valley snow is possible Friday evening into Saturday morning.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak upper low fades over Oregon Thursday and gives way to a ridge of dry air, so Washington's mountains stay quiet through Friday. Snow returns Saturday night as a weak system arrives, and Mt. Baker is the best bet for the following days, with 7 inches on Monday. Crystal Mountain and Stevens Pass see lighter snow through Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Light snow arrives from the west Thursday, then gets more organized Friday, mainly for the western mountains and passes. The system moves east and keeps snow going over higher elevations through the weekend. Grand Targhee leads with 3 inches on Friday, and Jackson Hole got 2 inches on Thursday. The NWS is calling for more, 12 to 25 inches at Grand Targhee Thursday night through Monday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Cypress Mountain and Whistler get mostly rain and a mix of rain and snow from Saturday through Tuesday, with wet weather through the week. Whistler is the better bet for snow, with 3 inches on Monday. Cypress is wetter, with a 4-inch day Monday that falls more as rain than snow.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A storm brings measurable snow to the mountains Thursday night into Saturday, with strong winds and blowing snow on Friday. Telluride leads with 6 inches on Friday, and Crested Butte got 2 inches the same day. Telluride's total is 9 inches. Fast-moving storms are possible through the Thanksgiving travel week, with timing still uncertain.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a trough will move into the West around Wednesday Nov 25, with mountain snow and possibly heavier rain in California into Wednesday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
